title: Throw what users can fix, rethrow the rest
prompt:
1. Finish `ValidationError` so instances have `name` set to `"ValidationError"` and a `field` property.
2. Make `parseAmount(text)` return whole cents, or throw a `ValidationError` with field `"amount"` when the text is empty, not a finite number, or not greater than 0.
3. Fix `tryAdd(list, label, amountText)`. For a valid entry it returns `{ ok: true, list }` with the new expense (trimmed label, amount in cents) added. An empty label throws a `ValidationError` with field `"label"`. Validation errors become `{ ok: false, field, message }`. **Any other error must be rethrown**, not swallowed.
hints: In the constructor, after `super(message)`: `this.name = "ValidationError"; this.field = field;`.
`Number("")` is 0 and `Number("Infinity")` is Infinity, so check `text.trim() === ""` and `Number.isFinite(dollars) && dollars > 0`.
In the `catch`: `if (error instanceof ValidationError) { return { ok: false, field: error.field, message: error.message }; } throw error;`.
explanation: `ValidationError` extends `Error`, so it keeps a message and a stack trace, and adds the `field` the form needs to place the message. `parseAmount` throws instead of returning a special value, so callers cannot accidentally treat a bad amount as a number. In `tryAdd`, the `catch` checks `instanceof ValidationError` and turns only those into a friendly result; anything else, such as the `TypeError` from spreading `null`, is a bug in the calling code and is rethrown so it shows up in the console instead of disappearing.

checks.error-class: `ValidationError` is an Error with a name and a field
checks.parse-ok: `parseAmount` returns whole cents for valid text
checks.parse-throws: `parseAmount` throws a ValidationError for empty, non-numeric, zero, negative or infinite input
checks.try-add-invalid: `tryAdd` returns { ok: false, field, message } for invalid input
checks.rethrows: `tryAdd` rethrows errors that are not ValidationErrors
